title: TVS' Lakshmi Venu seeks partition of family assets, escalating family feud
content:
Lakshmi Venu, a member of the TVS industrial family, has formally sought a partition of the joint family assets of her father Venu Srinivasan's branch, escalating a succession dispute that could have implications for ownership and control of key businesses within one of India's best-known automobile groups.
In a partition notice to her father, Lakshmi called on him, as head of the family, to discharge his fiduciary duties and ensure a "fair and lawful partition," according to a statement from her office on Monday.
Her mother, Mallika Srinivasan, has publicly backed her claim, exposing a deepening rift within the family over the distribution of its wealth.
Lakshmi maintains that she is entitled to an equal share under the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, as amended in 2005, and has an independent right to seek partition. She has invoked Section 6 of the Act, which recognises daughters as coparceners with the same rights as sons in qualifying Hindu joint family property.

title: FinMin examining suggestions for changes in equity capital gains tax: CBDT
content:
The Finance Ministry is examining various aspects of capital gains tax on equities, and probable changes in taxation would come in the Union Budget for 2027-28, a senior official said on Monday.
Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) Chairman Ravi Agrawal said the ministry is considering suggestions from various stakeholders made during the pre-budget meetings.
"We will consider it, and I'm sure on February 1 you will get to know. Analysis is being done of whatever issues have been flagged or points that have been raised by the stakeholders," Agrawal told reporters on the sidelines of the inauguration of a CBDT lounge at the IITF here.
Agrawal said the different facets of the capital gains tax regime, including tax implications, will be examined, and the decision will be announced in the Budget.
Industry chambers have already made representations to the Ministry recommending abolition of Long Term Capital Gains tax (LTCG).
They also suggested rationalising short-term capital gains .

title: Sebi may propose raising FPI beneficial ownership threshold to 25%
content:
Market regulator Sebi may propose raising the beneficial ownership identification threshold for foreign portfolio investors to 25 per cent from the current 10 per cent to ease compliance requirements and align India's regulatory framework with international best practices, an official said.
The regulator is examining several areas where Indian regulations may be unnecessarily intrusive, adding to compliance costs and making the country's markets less attractive.
"The regulator will soon issue another consultation paper outlining identified measures to simplify the compliance framework," he added.
Citing international benchmarking, the official said several developed and emerging jurisdictions follow a 25 per cent threshold for identifying beneficial ownership.
He said changes to certain provisions under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) and its rules would require government intervention, while Sebi could take up other measures through its consultation process.

content:
Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal on Monday urged the fintechs of India and Egypt to co-create and co-build cross-border payment systems to increase collaborations between entrepreneurs of the two countries.
He said both countries can look at facilitating entry of startups in each other's territories and participate in areas like government procurement.
Addressing Egypt-India Startup Forum here, he said India's UPI journey and Egypt's InstaPay share one vision.
"If our fintechs co-create, co-build cross-border payment systems riding on the technology created, coupled with local currencies trade in goods and services, that we have recently launched, can certainly help our trade to go up significantly and digital payments may get popular all across Egypt at almost no cost," Goyal said.

title: India's sugar output more than doubles to 2.35 mn tonnes by Nov 15: ISMA
content:
India's sugar production more than doubled to 23.59 lakh tonne in the ongoing 2026-27 season through November 15, as mills in top producer Maharashtra started crushing early, the Indian Sugar & Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association (ISMA) said on Monday.
Output stood at 11.49 lakh tonne in the same period a year earlier, the industry body said. The sugar season runs from October to September, with crushing typically starting in October-November.
The sweetener's production in Maharashtra, the country's biggest producer, jumped more than threefold to 18.51 lakh tonne from 5.25 lakh tonne a year earlier. Mills in the western state began crushing from October 8, earlier than in other states, and 154 mills were operating as of November 15, against 132 a year ago.
Output in Uttar Pradesh, the second-biggest producer, fell to 2.10 lakh tonne from 4.25 lakh tonne, with 80 mills operational compared with 88 a year earlier.
In Karnataka, the third-largest producer, output was little changed .

title: SC suspends life sentences, grants bail to 2 convicts in Bilkis Bano case
content:
The Supreme Court has suspended the life sentences of two convicts in the case of the gangrape of Bilkis Bano and murder of seven of her family members during the 2002 riots in Gujarat and granted them bail.
A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale noted that Bipin Chandra Joshi and Pradeep Mordhiya had been incarcerated for more than 17 years.
"Having heard the parties, suffice it to state that the appellants have been under incarceration for a period of more than 17 years, and also the fact remains that one of the appellants has a severe handicap. Certainly, there are issues to be decided in the appeal, both on fact and law," the apex court said in its October 28 order that has now been uploaded.
"In view of the above and considering the issues involved in this appeal, we suspend the sentence and grant bail to the appellants on such terms and conditions as may be imposed by the concerned trial court," the bench added.

title: Terrorist involved in attack on CRPF post killed in Kulgam encounter
content:
A terrorist was killed while another was trapped in an encounter with security forces in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam district where three CRPF personnel were injured in an attack last week, police said on Monday.
"Encounter with terrorists started in Kulgam," the Kashmir Zone Police said in a post on X.
The police said the whole area has been cordoned off with the help of the army and other security forces.
Officials identified the trapped terrorists as Lateef Bhatt and Umar. While the body of one terrorist was visible, efforts were on to neutralise the second terrorist.
The two terrorists were involved in the attack on a Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) post in the same district last week.
All the nearby units of the army and elite Special Operation Group of the Jammu and Kashmir Police were involved in the encounter.

title: Over 80% of servers were down at peak of global outage, says Microsoft
content:
More than 80 per cent of servers behind Microsoft's networking gateway were unresponsive at the peak of last week's global outage of Outlook and other Microsoft 365 services, the company has said, blaming a hidden software defect introduced in July.
Three factors together caused the outage of the networking gateway that sits in front of many Microsoft 365 services, Charles Lamanna, Microsoft's Executive Vice President of Copilot, Agents and Platform, said in a post on X on Monday.
"We are deeply sorry for the impact to all our customers and recognise the impact that this has on their normal business and operations," he said.
The first factor was a latent defect that caused servers to become overwhelmed and unresponsive under certain load conditions. It came from a fix prepared specifically for Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers and does not apply to broader Windows deployments, Lamanna said.

title: Muthoot FinCorp Q2 profit doubles to ₹779 crore on better asset quality
content:
Non-banking finance company Muthoot FinCorp Ltd has reported a two-fold jump in profit after tax to Rs 779 crore in the September quarter, driven by enhanced asset quality.
The company's profit after tax stood at Rs 388 crore in the July-September quarter of FY26.
Total income rose 71 per cent year-on-year to Rs 3,408 crore in the second quarter of FY27 from Rs 1,997 crore, Muthoot FinCorp, part of the Muthoot Pappachan Group, said in a regulatory filing.
On a sequential basis, Muthoot FinCorp's profit after tax rose 10.5 per cent from Rs 705 crore in the preceding June quarter, while total income increased 7.9 per cent from Rs 3,159 crore.
Asset quality also improved, with Stage III loan assets as a proportion of gross loan assets declining to 1.07 per cent as of September 2026 from 1.41 per cent year-earlier. Net Stage III loan assets fell to 0.63 per cent from 0.76 per cent.

title: Glenmark launches generic Inlyta tablets for kidney cancer treatment in US
content:
Glenmark Pharmaceuticals Inc, USA, on Monday announced the launch of Axitinib Tablets in 1 mg and 5 mg strengths, a generic version of Pfizer Inc's Inlyta tablets.
Glenmark Axitinib tablets (a generic equivalent to Pfizer's Inlyta) are used to treat advanced renal cell carcinoma (RCC), a type of kidney cancer.
"The launch of Axitinib tablets reinforces Glenmark's commitment to expanding access to quality, affordable medicines for patients in the United States," said Marc Kikuchi, President & Business Head, North America.
By adding this product to its portfolio, the company continues to strengthen focus on addressing the evolving needs of patients and healthcare providers, he said .
According to IQVIA sales data for the 12-month period ended September 2026, annual sales of Inlyta tablets in the US were around USD 538.4 million, the company said in a statement.

title: Trump's handpicked party chair faces a rebellion after midterm losses
content:
A nascent rebellion is underway against President Donald Trump's handpicked chairman at the Republican National Committee, and it's already getting ugly.
Some members are calling for a forensic audit of spending decisions, including hair and makeup services for Trump and other officials, as well as the hiring of the daughter of Trump's former chief of staff. Feuding Republicans are leaking emails and opposition research on rival factions. The White House is threatening to cut off fundraising assistance if the rebels don't fall in line.
The emerging fight, which will shape the 2028 presidential nominating contest, represents a rare challenge to Trump's dominance, even after the party's worst midterm performance in a generation. Despite the broad losses, Republican leaders across Washington have shown little desire to move past Trump and have largely stood behind his most unpopular policies.
